etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French fédéral, from Latin stem foeder- of foedus (“covenant, league, treaty, alliance”).

definitions.definition: Pertaining to a league or treaty; derived from an agreement or covenant between parties, especially between nations.

quote.citation: 1701, Nehemiah Grew, “Of Providence over Publick States”, in Cosmologia Sacra: Or A Discourse of the Universe as It is the Creature and Kingdom of God. […], London:  […]  W[illiam] Rogers, S[amuel] Smith, and B[enjamin] Walford: […], →OCLC, 3rd book, paragraph 27, page 113:
quote.text: Yet the Romans, taking them [the Carthaginians] at an Advantage, vvhen they vvere in Streights; compell'd them, contrary to all Fœderal Right and Juſtice, by Nevv Articles, both to part with Sardinia, their Lavvful Territory, and alſo to pay them for the future, a Double Tribute.

definitions.definition: Pertaining to the national government level in a federal nation, as opposed to state, provincial, county, city, or town.
(slang) Intrusive; airing out another's personal affairs.
(US) A law-enforcement official of the FBI
(US, historical) A unionist soldier in the American Civil War.
